options.text: X is a convex lens and Y is a concave lens.
X is a concave lens and Y is a convex lens.
Both are convex lenses because both outlines look curved.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: The diagram shows cross-sections of two transparent curved glass pieces, X and Y. Harsh compares thickness at the middle with thickness near the edges of each piece.

part_answers.answer: A convex lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges (X); a concave lens is thicker at the edges than in the middle (Y).

teacher.key_rationale: Thickness pattern classifies the lenses: thicker middle is convex (X); thicker edges is concave (Y). Swapping names or judging only from a curved outline is wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source converging-lens ray diagram into two labelled lens cross-sections X (thicker middle) and Y (thicker edges).
